current.text: He enters the season healthy after his first healthy offseason in years. He reportedly added 15 pounds of muscle.
Yahoo lists him as questionable for rest.
Because he is healthy, one expert projects him at 33 minutes per game.
He is expected to play about 40 to 50 games this season.
He is the projected starting center, next to Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown and LeBron James.
Philadelphia added Jaylen Brown and LeBron James.
Usage on the team must shrink. Maxey, Brown, James and Embiid will cut into each other's shots and touches.

He is projected at about 20 to 25 points and about 10 rebounds per game, with some big scoring games. He is seen as an emergency scorer who gets to the free throw line and rebounds, while others carry most of the scoring.
The Sixers have only 13 back-to-backs, but three of them fall in the fantasy playoffs. He is not expected to play back-to-backs, so he should miss games in those weeks.
Philadelphia is projected to win about 51 to 52 games. Expect growing pains in October and November and load management for the stars.
Experts agree he should not go inside the top 50. Around picks 56 to 64 is a fair price, or a good one, for a player who starts the season healthy.
One expert expects him to finish around rank 60 and to do more than last season. He calls ESPN's rank of 88 thievery.
He is a high-risk pick with about a 10% chance of working out, but a big payoff if it does.
In a mock auction he went for 16 USD, and Josh would not bid on him at all.

durable.text: He has a long history of knee problems and surgeries. He is often questionable and misses many games.
Experts have low hopes for his long-term health. Josh avoids him for that reason.
His per-game line is near the top of the league. He ranked 11th per game last season, so the question is how many games he plays, not how well.
As an often-injured player, he is worth a bit less in head-to-head leagues like ours than in roto.
Points and FT% are league-outlier strengths. His FT% comes on high volume, so it clearly lifts a team's FT%.
Turnovers are his weak category. He has many turnovers, even for a center.
Nick Nurse plays his starters very heavy minutes.

note: He is a strong per-game asset in points and FT%, but he costs you in turnovers and may only play 40 to 50 games. In head-to-head that leaves empty weeks, especially in our playoffs, where the Sixers have three back-to-backs. The market values him at about pick 56 to 64. Yahoo average cost (7.3 USD) and ESPN average cost (8 USD) are well below our league's 24 USD last season and the 16 USD mock auction price. Treat Yahoo's 19 USD value as the most you would pay. He fits punt TO builds that want FT% and points from a center. Early on, check how many games he plays and whether LeBron James and Jaylen Brown cut his shots.
